items.text: AMEND (T) AND RECOMMIT TO ENVIRONMENTAL CONSERVATION

items.actClause:
AN ACT to establish a commission to be known as the "New York seawall study
commission"; and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration
thereof
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1812

SPONSOR: ADDABBO
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to establish a commission to be known as the "New York seawall
study commission"; and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon
expiration thereof

 
PURPOSE:

To set up a commission to study the feasibility, costs, impacts, and
best locations for construction of a seawall around the city of New
York's coastline.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

The Commission shall consist of members who shall be appointed as
follows:

The Commissioner of Environmental Conservation or his/her designee; The
Secretary of State or his/her designee;

3 members appointed by the Governor at least 1 of whom shall have exper-
tise in environmental justice issues;

2 members to be appointed by the Temporary President of the Senate; 2
members to be appointed by the Speaker of the Assembly;

1 member to be appointed by the Minority Leader of the Senate; 1 member
to be appointed by the Minority leader of the Assembly; 2 members to be
appointed by the Mayor of New York City; 1 member to be appointed by the
County Executive of. Nassau; 1 member to be appointed by the County
Executive of Suffolk; and, 1 member to be appointed by the County Execu-
tive of Westchester Members should include individuals with expertise in
one or more of the following areas: climatology; hydrology; environ-
mental; aquaculture; flood risk management; environmental justice;
ecological restoration and management; or coastal ocean science; and
engineering.

By December 31, 2023 the Commission shall deliver to the Governor and
Legislature a report to include:

Coastal areas at greatest risk from sea level rise; Areas at risk from
storm surge based on current sea levels; Areas that are more likely to
be at risk from coastal hazards, including from extreme weather events,
with projections extending through year 2100; Locations for construction
of a seawall including -any communities to he at risk from such
construction; Feasibility, costs and locations of nature-based solutions
and on shore protection measures; Costs including impacts to vulnerable
populations and natural resources; and, Recommendations on state and
local regulatory and/or statutory alterations

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In just the last few years, we have seen one horrific storm after anoth-
er. These once in a lifetime storms are becoming more and more common.
New York City must be prepared for the next Hurricane Sandy.  A seawall
is one idea that could possibly save lives in the next super-storm, as
well as protect vital infrastructure that could cost billions to repair.
This piece of legislation would create a commission to study the New
York City coastline to determine the feasibility of a seawall. In 1900,
a Category 4 hurricane, the "Great Storm", struck Galveston, Texas kill-
ing 6,000 to 12,000 individuals.  It was the deadliest natural disaster
in U.S history. In 1915, a similar storm in strength struck Galveston,
but the seawall proved invaluable for protection of-the city and its
residents. A seawall as seen in Galveston, can help save lives and
protect infrastructure. A study of how such a seawall can be of vital
service to the New York City coast makes perfect sense.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2020: S.8841 - Referred to Rules.

2021: S. 7141 - Referred to Rules.

2022:

 
FISCAL IMPACT:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

A.actClause:
AN ACT to require the department of environmental conservation to conduct a
study on the feasibility of constructing a seawall along the coastline of the
city of New York; and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon
expiration thereof
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1812A   Revised 1/16/24

SPONSOR: ADDABBO
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to require the department of environmental conservation to
conduct a study on the feasibility of constructing a seawall along the
coastline of the city of New York; and providing for the repeal of such
provisions upon expiration thereof

 
PURPOSE:

To supplement existing study efforts of the feasibility, costs, impacts,
and best locations for construction of protective measures for the city
of New York.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 requires the Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) to
study the feasibility, costs, impacts, and, if applicable, best
locations for construction of a seawall to protect the city of New fork
from sea level rise and storm surge.

The study is due no later than December 31, 2027, and shall be in the
form of a report containing the following: (a) coastal areas at greatest
risk from sea level rise based on projections established pursuant to
section 3-0319 of the environmental conservation law; (b) areas at risk
from storm surge based on current sea levels; (c) areas that are more
likely to be at risk from coastal hazards including rising groundwater
levels, saltwater intrusion, coastal flooding, and extreme weather
events including coastal storms, with such projections extending through
year 2100; (d) the locations for construction of a seawall and any
communities likely to be at risk from such construction; (e) the feasi-
bility, costs and locations of natural and nature-based solutions and
onshore measures to protect New York city from sea level rise and storm
surge; (f) the costs, including fiscal impacts, impacts on vulnerable
populations and natural resources, of such construction of a seawall;
and (g) recommendations on state and local regulatory and/or statutory
alterations.

Section 2. Effective date, and expiration date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In just the last few years, we have seen one horrific storm after anoth-
er. These once in a lifetime storms are becoming more and more common.
New York City must be prepared for the next Hurricane Sandy. Seawalls
and other measures could possibly save lives in the next super-storm, as
well as protect vital infrastructure that could cost billions to repair.
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (the "Corps"), is working with New York
City, New York State, and New Jersey to studying and develop options for
protecting the New York Harbor from the consequences of climate change
impacts such as storm surge and storms. To that end, the Corps in 2022
released plans to build sea gates and other protective measures. A vari-
ety of concerns have been raised regarding the Corps' proposal, and in
November of 2023, the Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC)
requested that the Corps revisit its proposal more holistically (an
additional letter to the same effect was sent to the Corps from both New
York and New Jersey in early January 2024).
This legislation would require DEC to study the the feasibility of a
seawall and examine the appropriateness of other protective measures.
While the state is a continuing partner in efforts to protect New York
Harbor being led by the Corps, this study could supplement and inform
that work, and further New York's expressed concerns and objectives.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2020: S.8841 - Referred to Rules.

2021: S.7141 - Referred to Rules.

2022: S.7141 - Vetoed, tabled

2023: S1812 - Passed Senate

 
FISCAL IMPACT:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately and shall expire and be deemed
repealed January 1, 2028.

summary: Requires the department of environmental conservation to conduct a study on the feasibility of constructing a seawall along the coastline of the city of New York and report on such study to the legislature by December 31, 2027.
